citations.label: Supported capabilities (iOS) - Reference - Account - Help - Apple Developer

result.answer_markdown:
**No. With a free Apple Personal Team, your iPhone app cannot get remote push notifications — not while it is closed and not while it is open.**

Remote push notifications work through a permission called the Push Notifications capability. That capability adds an item to the app's provisioning profile — the file Apple gives your app that lists what it is allowed to do. The item is named `aps-environment`, and it is what lets the app ask Apple's Push Notification service (APNs) for a device token. That token is the address Apple needs to deliver a notification to your specific phone. A free Personal Team profile cannot contain this item. Apple lists supported capabilities for iOS accounts in [Supported capabilities (iOS) - Reference - Account - Help - Apple Developer](https://developer.apple.com/help/account/reference/supported-capabilities-ios/), and Push Notifications is not available to free profiles.

Because there is no entitlement, your app never receives a device token. Without a token, Apple has no address to send to, so nothing arrives from APNs — not when the app is in the background, and not when it is open. This is not a setting you can fix in your code.

Two related points are worth knowing. Local notifications still work: these are notifications your own app schedules on the phone itself, and they do not need APNs or the capability. And to use remote push at all, you need a paid Apple Developer Program membership. A separate limit is that free profiles expire after 7 days, so the app must be reinstalled or rebuilt to keep running.
